rejected.title: Private health insurance
card: Private health insurance is optional. People pay a premium to an insurer, which then pays part or all of some health costs.
pays for care as a private patient in a hospital, such as choosing your doctor or having a private room. Medicare still covers public hospital care for everyone.
pays part of services that Medicare mostly does not cover, such as dental, physiotherapy and glasses.

The government encourages people to buy cover. The private health insurance rebate lowers the premium for many people. The Medicare levy surcharge is an extra charge on some higher earners who do not have hospital cover.
rejected.remember: Private cover is a choice, and the government uses a rebate and a levy to push people towards it.

a.q: Which statement best describes private health insurance in Australia?
opts: An optional cover that pays for some private care and extras
A compulsory scheme paid for through the Medicare levy
A scheme that only lowers the cost of prescription medicines
A service that replaces public hospital care for members
a.why: People choose whether to buy private cover, and it pays towards private hospital care and extras. It is not compulsory, and Medicare still covers public hospital care for everyone, so it does not replace it.
a.clue: Think about whether anyone has to buy it.

b.q: Jonas, 35, earns a high income in Geelong and has no private hospital cover. Which government measure is meant to encourage him to buy it?
opts: The Medicare levy surcharge, an extra charge for no cover
The private health insurance rebate, which he is paying now
The Medicare levy, which is waived once cover is bought
A fine that every person without cover must pay
b.why: The Medicare levy surcharge applies to some higher earners without hospital cover, which gives them a reason to buy it. The rebate lowers premiums for people who already hold cover, so it cannot apply to Jonas as he has none. The surcharge is not a fine on everyone without cover.
b.clue: Which measure is an extra charge for higher earners?
